scopeStatement: This reconstructs only what the supplied 156.367-second video, supplied SRT, generated frame evidence, Vision OCR, and locally derived inspection notes establish. It does not externally verify the presenter's claims about creators, AI, platforms, traffic, account weight, or account launching.

viewerChange.before: The intended viewer may treat AI as a shortcut that can author self-media content, launch an account, or generate a viral post with one click.
viewerChange.after: The intended viewer is pushed to distrust one-click promises and seller incentives, prioritize a human-selected topic and empathy, treat traffic as incompletely reproducible, consider the author's claimed quality/weight risks, and use AI only as support for knowledge gaps or brainstorming rather than as a replacement author.

limitations: Each frame proves only its instant.
The manifest does not itself interpret visual content.
OCR is a proposal, not ground truth.
Handwritten whiteboard text is often low-confidence or wrong.

derivedSources.kind: human frame check of OCR proposals
derivedSources.producedBy: manual comparison of each accepted OCR row with its full-resolution targeted frame
limitations: Exact small whiteboard text remains mostly unknown.

derivedSources.kind: audio stream and non-speech-channel inspection note
derivedSources.producedBy: ffprobe, ffmpeg silencedetect/volumedetect, and Whisper machine transcription
limitations: Methods did not reliably separate speech from music or sound effects.
Especially unreliable for the opening fragment and some homophones.

derivedSources.producedBy: manual inspection of all supplied cues, cue/shot/dense frames, targeted frames, OCR, whiteboard, environment, and audio metadata
limitations: Applies only to the inspected video-internal scope.
Unreadable microtext and handwritten text remain unknown.

knowledgeUnits.title: Opening proof-like collage
knowledgeUnits.statement: During the first 0.733 seconds, an inserted collage covers much of the presenter and shows multiple large engagement/view-style numbers, including 611.9万, 832.7万, and 976.0万浏览, framing the masked presenter with visual credibility before the thesis.

evidence.supports: Opening collage with many count labels.

knowledgeUnits.reasoning: The numbers and collage are directly visible; their platform, ownership, authenticity, and attribution are not established.

knowledgeUnits.title: Contrarian opening thesis
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author opens by telling viewers not to use AI to make self-media content, launch an account, or attempt viral posts.

evidence.supports: Checked burned caption: 就是不要用AI做自媒体.

unknowns: The hook's broad wording is narrowed at the close.

knowledgeUnits.title: Audience and controversy qualifier
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author says the video is only for people with dialectical and open logic and predicts it will offend people already using AI for self-media and peers preparing to make money from AI.

knowledgeUnits.title: Promoter-incentive critique
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author claims that people encouraging AI-based self-media are motivated to sell agents, skills, and mini-programs and thereby earn the viewer's money.

argument.claim: AI promoters recommend AI to sell products to the viewer.
conditions: applies to the promoters the author generalizes about
limits: No named promoter or motive evidence is shown.

unknowns: truth and scope of the motive attribution

knowledgeUnits.title: Profile test: poor data
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author's first profile test is: if the promoter's own data are poor, the viewer has no reason to listen.
unknowns: No threshold for poor data is defined.

knowledgeUnits.title: Profile test: good data and authorship assertion
knowledgeUnits.statement: For the good-data branch, the author asserts that the promoter's viral posts definitely were not made by AI and broadens this to say no real blogger uses AI to do self-media.
knowledgeUnits.argumentNodeRole: decision rule branch B and universal claim

argument.claim: Good-performing examples on promoters' profiles were not AI-made, and real bloggers do not use AI for self-media.
limits: No authorship audit or creator sample is shown.

knowledgeUnits.title: What is closest to a viral post
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author's positive alternative is to do the thing closest to virality: find a good topic that reaches deeply into human concerns, then begin writing.
unknowns: No method for evaluating a good topic is supplied.

knowledgeUnits.title: One-click promise versus account-specific adaptation
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author calls a promise of one-click viral output nonsense because, although self-media has underlying logic, every account and IP requires case-specific analysis; he says adapting a suitable AI would itself take time.

argument.claim: A one-click viral generator is not credible.
actions: spend time adapting an AI if choosing to use one
limits: No named system or adaptation procedure is demonstrated.

knowledgeUnits.title: Traffic is patterned but not reliably repeatable
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author says traffic has patterns whose outcomes remain irregular: reposting the same viral item may not work because timing, place, and people matter; viral posts can be analyzed but sometimes cannot be reproduced.

evidence.supports: Same post may not repeat success.

unknowns: No repost comparison data are shown.

knowledgeUnits.title: Human nature and empathy rationale
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author claims that content is fundamentally about human nature and making content is fundamentally about empathy; trying to use a machine to empathize with humans is, in his words, contempt for humans.
unknowns: The video does not test whether AI-assisted content can evoke empathy.

knowledgeUnits.title: AI short-video qualification and 60-point claim
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author explicitly says he is not declaring that AI cannot make short videos; he says it can make short videos, but characterizes them as only 60-point videos and says such a video is not worth posting.

knowledgeUnits.title: Different risk for novices and established bloggers
knowledgeUnits.statement: For a novice trying to launch an account, the author says a 60-point video is useless; for an established blogger, he says it is even less acceptable because of account weight.
unknowns: No operational weight metric is defined.

knowledgeUnits.title: Million-follower weight hypothetical
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author gives a hypothetical: a million-follower blogger whose normal good content averages 50,000 likes may, after several consecutive 3,000-like videos, be judged by the platform as careless and have weight and base distribution reduced, allegedly faster than a low-follower user.

evidence.supports: Checked 3,000 caption with documented OCR correction.

argument.claim: Low-performing posts can reduce an established creator's weight and base distribution.
conditions: several consecutive 3,000-like videos against a 50,000-like baseline
limits: No analytics or platform rule is shown.
The example is not empirical proof.

knowledgeUnits.title: Account launch as breakthrough, not accumulation
knowledgeUnits.statement: The author claims that launching an account is not gradual accumulation but overnight fame; he rejects a slow-rising curve and says a later hit is not the reward for persistence but evidence that the creator finally understood how to make better content.

evidence.supports: Checked slow-rising-curve caption with documented correction.

unknowns: No account trajectory or causal study is shown.

knowledgeUnits.title: Permitted AI support
knowledgeUnits.statement: At the close, the author permits using AI during writing to fill knowledge gaps and to chat for brainstorming.
unknowns: How much AI assistance remains acceptable is not specified.

knowledgeUnits.title: Prohibited AI substitution
knowledgeUnits.statement: The closing prohibition is to have AI generate a script with one click and then directly film from that script.

knowledgeUnits.title: Opening-to-closing semantic relation
knowledgeUnits.statement: The closing narrows the opening's broad 'do not use AI for self-media' hook into an assistance-versus-substitution boundary: brainstorming and gap-filling are allowed, while delegated one-click authorship is rejected.

evidence.supports: Prohibited direct filming from generated script.

knowledgeUnits.reasoning: The ending does not simply repeat the hook; it defines permitted and prohibited uses, so the global relation is narrowing/qualification rather than contradiction or repetition.
knowledgeUnits.openingClosingFunction: hook narrowed by final operational boundary

knowledgeUnits.title: Whiteboard and gestures as argument aids
knowledgeUnits.statement: Across the lesson, the presenter repeatedly points to a prewritten whiteboard outline and later adds or indicates simple decline and curve drawings while explaining weight and account-launch trajectories; the board visually groups the argument but most small handwriting is not reliably readable.

evidence.supports: Presenter points to the persistent outline.
Later diagram state during breakthrough explanation.

knowledgeUnits.visualArgumentAid: outline, pointing, decline marks, gradual versus sudden curve

knowledgeUnits.title: Masked recurring presenter referent
knowledgeUnits.statement: A single recurring visible presenter wears a red-and-black superhero-like full-face mask, dark jacket, printed shirt, and microphone, alternately addressing the camera and whiteboard; this visible person is the speaking presenter, but literal identity and mask authorization are not established.

evidence.supports: Recurring masked presenter in whiteboard room.
Same presentational referent through long middle interval.

knowledgeUnits.referentAndIdentityBoundary: visible speaker stands in for the author/presenter; personal identity unknown

knowledgeUnits.title: SRT closing self-label
knowledgeUnits.statement: The supplied SRT records the closing self-label as 我是人类智商编导, followed by 下课.
unknowns: Whether this exactly matches the audible word is not established by direct human audition here.

knowledgeUnits.title: Burned-caption closing self-label
knowledgeUnits.statement: The visible burned caption at 155.15 seconds reads 我是人类最强编导, followed by a separate 下课 caption.

evidence.supports: Full-resolution frame visibly reads 我是人类最强编导.
Vision OCR proposal exactly matches the checked frame.

knowledgeUnits.title: Closing label remains carrier-conflicted
knowledgeUnits.statement: A single carrier-unified closing label cannot be established: the burned caption says 人类最强编导, while the supplied SRT and machine audio transcript say 人类智商编导. Only the masked presenter's self-brand/persona function and the classroom sign-off are secure across the close.

evidence.supports: Machine audition also proposes 智商; limited by recognition uncertainty.

knowledgeUnits.reasoning: The raw forms conflict and are not silently normalized.
knowledgeUnits.carrierConflictResolution: unresolved 最强 versus 智商

knowledgeUnits.title: Source technical segmentation
knowledgeUnits.statement: The evidence pack divides the video into 11 technical shot-detection segments, including a sub-second opening insert and a final 0.1-second tail.

knowledgeUnits.title: Semantic continuity across technical boundaries
knowledgeUnits.statement: Paired frames around the detected boundaries show the same masked presenter, clothing, whiteboard, room, and camera axis through most of the video; after the opening insert, the content is one continuous whiteboard argument rather than 11 evidenced semantic scenes. Hidden cuts remain possible.

evidence.supports: After closing boundary with same room/presenter.

knowledgeUnits.technicalSegmentationVersusSemanticConti: technical boundaries not equivalent to semantic scenes or confirmed edit count

knowledgeUnits.title: Decision-relevant boundaries not established
knowledgeUnits.statement: Within the inspected 0-156.367-second video-internal scope, no specific AI product/version, platform, price, access route, account requirement, region, support/responsibility entity, demonstrated product workflow, or empirical proof for the universal/causal claims was observed.

evidence.supports: Bounded full-timeline review, carriers checked, sought items, and limitations.

knowledgeUnits.scopedAbsenceAndUnknown: not observed in the inspected full timeline and listed carriers only
unknowns: all listed decision boundaries and empirical truth

knowledgeUnits.title: Non-speech audio role remains unknown
knowledgeUnits.statement: The video has a continuous AAC audio stream carrying speech, but the available inspection did not reliably separate or identify an independent semantic role for music or sound effects; their presence or absence must not be asserted.

evidence.supports: Audio stream metadata, continuous-material observation, and separation limitation.

knowledgeUnits.title: Raw opening SRT fragment
knowledgeUnits.statement: The supplied SRT begins with the raw phrase 太多展示教资，今天我只说一件事情.

knowledgeUnits.title: Visible opening insert label
knowledgeUnits.statement: The opening collage visibly contains the text 开头展示教资, which labels the insert and is not sufficient to establish the exact spoken phrase under it.

evidence.supports: Full-resolution insert visibly reads 开头展示教资.

knowledgeUnits.carrierConflictResolution: insert text kept separate from speech/SRT

knowledgeUnits.title: Opening initial phrase unresolved
knowledgeUnits.statement: The exact audible first phrase before 今天我只说一件事情 remains unknown: the SRT's 太多展示教资, the insert's 开头展示教资, and the machine transcription's different low-confidence proposal cannot be collapsed into one reading.

evidence.supports: Only the later phrase 今天我只说一件事情 is visually secure.
Machine transcription proposes another uncertain form.

knowledgeUnits.reasoning: Multiple carriers disagree and none establishes the initial audible phrase with sufficient reliability.

Good topic versus buying AI transition.

metaGate.question: 原视频还有哪种信息载体、意义变化或知识关系根本没被协议检查？
metaGate.rationale: All ten available carrier groups were inspected or, for non-speech audio, explicitly inspected and preserved as semantically unknown. All 12 probe meaning changes, 10 probe relationship hypotheses, 17 critical questions, 56 cues, the opening collage, closing reframe, two consequential carrier conflicts, referents, scoped absences, and technical-segmentation/semantic-continuity distinction are represented. No relation is a self-edge.
